basis: Acquired dermal pigment deposition, usually after topical hydroquinone; tissue discoloration alone does not establish ocular or cartilage dysfunction.
Inherited sinus-node dysfunction; associated arrhythmias, ventricular noncompaction and valve abnormalities remain cardiovascular.
Inherited copper homeostasis disorders; neurologic, hepatic and connective-tissue injury vary substantially by subtype without an established group-wide frequency.
The definition specifies SMAD7-associated colorectal cancer, establishing intestinal tumor origin despite the susceptibility wording.
Joubert brain malformation and developmental impairment; persistent ptosis in 15/18 supports ocular involvement. Thoracic and pulmonary hypoplasia each occur in 4/19.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with defining brain malformations and developmental impairment, plus severe structural and functional eye disease.
Craniosynostosis and arthrogryposis define skeletal disease; cleft palate is an oral structural defect. No evidence establishes additional organ injury.
Isolated microphthalmia with iris coloboma and possible cataract; all established manifestations are ocular.
Microcephaly defines abnormal brain development. Growth restriction and chromatid exchange alone do not establish endocrine, skeletal or blood disease across this umbrella.
Bradykinin-mediated angioedema affects subcutis, oral tissues and the upper airway as defining sites; this drug reaction is not inherently immune-mediated.
Inherited cytotoxic immune failure with hemophagocytosis and cytopenias; hepatic inflammation occurs in most, and CNS inflammation affects roughly 30-60% in familial HLH.
Oocyte maturation and zygotic cleavage failure cause reproductive infertility without established endocrine gland dysfunction or another covered axis.
Reactive leukocytosis with immature neutrophils defines a blood abnormality; the definition does not support the erroneous plasma-cell-neoplasm ancestry.
Glycosylation disorder with hepatic injury markers in 8/8 and factor XI deficiency in 6/6; isolated small-denominator reports do not establish other common organ injury.
An eosinophilic systemic disorder; hypereosinophilic-syndrome and restrictive-cardiomyopathy ancestry support blood and cardiac disease. Other organ frequencies are unspecified.
Inherited peripheral axonal neuropathy; established distal amyotrophy in 16/17 and persistent foot deformities in about half support musculoskeletal involvement.
Basal cell carcinoma originates in penile skin, usually the shaft; the covered organ is skin despite its genital location.
Localized coccygeal disorder, commonly following direct skeletal injury; pain alone does not establish an additional neurologic disease.
Structural hair-shaft dysplasia with segmental branching; hair belongs to the dermatologic axis.
A germ-cell tumor arising in the testis; reproductive tumor origin does not establish endocrine dysfunction or another covered axis.
A mature B-cell lymphoplasmacytic malignancy, commonly involving marrow; lymphoma requires the infectious_immune mechanism axis regardless of IgM production.
Complex I metabolic disease with cardiomyopathy and encephalopathy; hepatic steatosis occurs in 30-79%. Common myopathy and thrombocytopenia omitted under the four-axis cap.
Progressive retinal dysfunction with night blindness and visual loss; associated hearing impairment is occasional, below 30%.
Parathyroid tumors and ossifying jaw fibromas define the syndrome. Intrinsic renal cysts/neoplasms usually affect <30%; stones and nephrocalcinosis are separate complications.
Benign tumor of the buccal mucosa; oral mucosa belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
